anomalies.observed: On both ADM3260 bridges the wet-chemistry probe data lines (M2/M3 RX/SDA,TX/SCL, which sit in the isolated VDDISO/GNDISO domain) are wired to pins 18/19 = SDA1/SCL1, while the non-isolated ESP32 bus I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL is wired to pins 3/2 = SDA2/SCL2. In the ADM3260 datasheet SDA1/SCL1 are the PRIMARY (VDDP/VIN) side and SDA2/SCL2 are the ISOLATED (VISO/VDDISO/GNDISO) side, so the symbol's pin grouping (SDA1/SCL1 drawn beside VISO/VDDISO) is wrong and the designer wired the two domains to opposite sides of the isolation barrier.
anomalies.expected: Spec §4.2: 'U3 (pH) and U4 (EC) each present a secondary isolated I2C pair (/SDA_pH//SCL_pH, /SDA_EC//SCL_EC) that connects directly to M2 (EZO-pH) and M3 (EZO-EC)'; the primary (non-isolated) side must carry I2C_SDA/I2C_SCL. The probes should be on SDA2/SCL2 and the MCU bus on SDA1/SCL1.

anomalies.impact: Galvanic isolation between the ESP32/digital ground and the wet pH/EC probes is defeated (the probe signals are referenced to the primary side and the MCU bus to the isolated side), so the probes are no longer isolated from ground loops and the isolated I2C link is likely non-functional.

anomalies.observed: The main-pump low-side N-MOSFET T2 (IRLR2905) has its gate node pulled UP to +3V3 through R5 (10 k). The structurally identical ATO-valve driver instead pulls its gate node DOWN to GND through R12 (10 k).
anomalies.expected: A low-side N-MOSFET switch must have a gate pull-DOWN to GND so it is OFF by default and OFF when the MCU/level-shifter is not driving it (as R12 does for T5). Spec §2 describes T2 as a low-side switch 'pre-driven via T1 (BT3904)' for the main circulation pump, with a float-switch low-level cutoff interlock.

evidence.quote: Page 1/3, MAIN PUMP: R5 10k top to +3V3, bottom to T1 collector / T2 gate node; ATO VALVE: R12 10k bottom to GND, top to T4 collector / T5 gate node
§2: 'T2 — IRLR2905 ... Main circulation-pump low-side switch ... gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) from the ESP32 pin, pre-driven via T1 (BT3904) NPN level shifter'

anomalies.impact: The main circulation pump is energised by default (gate held high when T1 is off) and the low-water float interlock inverts: pulling T1's base low turns the pump ON instead of OFF, defeating the safety cutoff.

anomalies.observed: R6 (10 k) is connected as a pull-UP to +3V3 on the FLOAT_HIGH net, and R9 (10 k) as a pull-DOWN to GND on the FLOAT_LOW net. The float switches are wired SW1: VCC↔HIGH and SW2: LOW↔GND, so FLOAT_HIGH is an active-high signal (needs a pull-down) and FLOAT_LOW is active-low (needs a pull-up).
anomalies.expected: Spec §4.4 .cir: 'R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k' and 'R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k' — i.e. R6 pulls FLOAT_LOW up and R9 pulls FLOAT_HIGH down.

evidence.quote: Page 1, WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES: R6 10k between +3V3 and FLOAT_HIGH line; R9 10k between GND and FLOAT_LOW line

anomalies.impact: Both float switches read a constant level (HIGH stuck high, LOW stuck low), so low/high water detection fails and the R2/R11 hardware interlocks to the pump and ATO drivers sit at the wrong default potential.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended design in the isolated-I2C and pump/valve driver sections: the ADM3260 bridges (U3/U4) have their primary and isolated I2C channels swapped relative to their power domains (defeating probe galvanic isolation), the main-pump MOSFET gate is pulled up to +3V3 instead of down to GND (default-ON pump with inverted low-water cutoff), and the float-switch pull resistors R6/R9 are tied to the opposite nets than specified.
